prerequisites: Knowledge of high school mathematics is sufficient.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the principles of Geometry and Linear Algebra, as essential tools for the theoretical construction and practical resolution of typical engineering models.
Know the basic aspects of Linear Algebra and Geometry.
Be able to analyze the important aspects of a function of an engineering problem and solve it using Linear Algebra.
Be able to independently apply the theorems of Geometry and Algebra to the resolution of engineering problems.
Be able to describe, with a sufficient level of formalism and appropriate language, a theorem or the resolution of a problem.
Be able, given a problem, to evaluate the different resolution strategies and choose the most suitable one in specific circumstances, aware of the limitations and strengths of the adopted strategy.

syllabus_topics: Vector spaces and their elementary properties
Numerical vector space and that of free vectors
Ladder matrices and Gauss-Jordan algorithm, rank
Invertible matrices, calculating the inverse of a matrix
Systems of linear equations, solving systems of linear ladder equations
Reduction of a system of linear equations to a ladder system
Theorem of the kernel and of the image
Parametric and Cartesian representation of subspaces
Orthogonal bases, existence of orthogonal bases
Components of a Vector with Respect to an Orthonormal Basis
Determination of eigenvalues, characteristic polynomial, algebraic and geometric multiplicity
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a compulsory written exam and an oral exam. The final grade is given by a score, with a maximum possible score equal to 30. The oral exam may be taken by students who have passed the written exam.
